page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The server features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only cached blocks reaching 7392.56 GB/sec and uncached large blocks reaching 459.25 GB/sec. Multi-core capabilities are strong, as demonstrated by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scoring, software compilation with Clang, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, with Redis achieving 133.11 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression remain in the average tier.

Given the high density of dedicated physical ARM cores and integrated local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio limits its suitability for memory-bound applications requiring massive datasets in RAM, but the top-tier memory bandwidth and local NVMe storage mitigate this for disk-heavy operations. It is suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
